# pantechdynamics_kubernetes_node_pool (Resource)

A group of workers of a pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster with its own plan, size, Kubernetes labels and taints, for example bigger nodes for a database, or nodes only some workloads may use. Every worker is a VM of node_plan, joined with the pool's labels, the label pantech.io/node-pool=<name> and the pool's taints, so a workload picks the pool with a nodeSelector and tolerations. Each worker is billed as a VM of node_plan once it has joined the cluster (observed_workers). With autoscaling, the platform adds a worker when a pod the pool could run is waiting for room, and removes the newest one after 10 idle minutes. In a zone where every node has one fixed size (af-abj-2: 2 vCPU, 4 GB) the plan must be that size, or the create fails with KUBERNETES_PLAN_NOT_IN_ZONE. Create waits until every worker has joined. workers and autoscaling change in place; changing anything else replaces the pool.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Workers of their own plan; each is billed as a VM of that plan once it has
# joined the cluster (observed_workers).

# Bigger workers only database pods may use: they must tolerate the taint and
# can select the nodes by the label.
resource "pantechdynamics_kubernetes_node_pool" "db" {
  cluster_id = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.id
  name       = "db"
  node_plan  = "s-4vcpu-8gb" # each worker is billed as a VM of this plan
  workers    = 2             # changes in place

  labels = { role = "db" }
  taints = [{ key = "dedicated", value = "db", effect = "NoSchedule" }]
}

# Workers the autoscaler keeps between 1 and 5, starting at 1.
resource "pantechdynamics_kubernetes_node_pool" "burst" {
  cluster_id = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.id
  name       = "burst"
  node_plan  = "s-2vcpu-4gb"
  autoscaling = {
    enabled     = true
    min_workers = 1
    max_workers = 5
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Id of the cluster, starting with k8s_. It must be running. Changing it replaces the pool.
- `name` (String) Name of the pool, 1 to 63 characters, unique in the cluster. Changing it replaces the pool.
- `node_plan` (String) Slug of the plan every worker of the pool uses, from the pantechdynamics_plans data source. The API reports the plan only by id (node_plan_id), so after an import this holds no value. Changing it replaces the pool.

### Optional

- `autoscaling` (Attributes) The autoscaler, which keeps the pool between min_workers and max_workers. Changes in place. Removing it (or enabled = false) turns it off at the current count, or at workers when set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling))
- `labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes labels set on every node of the pool, for example { role = "db" }. Changing them replaces the pool.
- `taints` (Attributes List) Kubernetes taints set on every node of the pool, so only pods that tolerate them run there. Changing them replaces the pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--taints))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `workers` (Number) A fixed number of workers, 1 to 10. Required unless autoscaling is enabled; with it, the pool starts here (or at min_workers when unset) and the autoscaler then owns the count, which never causes a diff. Changes in place.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the pool was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the node pool, starting with k8spool_.
- `node_plan_id` (String) Id of the plan every worker uses.
- `observed_workers` (Number) The pool's workers that have joined the cluster. This is what is billed.
- `status` (String) What the cluster runs of the pool: "provisioning" (workers being built), "ready" (every worker has joined), "updating" (a scale in progress), "deleting", or "unavailable" (a pool made while node pools were a preview, with no node size: replace it).

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the autoscaler runs. false is the same as leaving autoscaling out.

Optional:

- `max_workers` (Number) Most workers, min_workers to 10. Required when enabled.
- `min_workers` (Number) Fewest workers, 1 to 10. Required when enabled.


<a id="nestedatt--taints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `taints`

Required:

- `effect` (String) "NoSchedule", "PreferNoSchedule" or "NoExecute".
- `key` (String) The taint's key.
- `value` (String) The taint's value.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A node pool is imported as "<cluster_id>/<pool_id>". node_plan cannot be read
# back: set it in the configuration.
terraform import pantechdynamics_kubernetes_node_pool.db k8s_06ggex1abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw/k8spool_06ggex1abcdefghjkmnpqrst
```
